In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a least squares cubic method for determining the relationship between δ18O and deuterium in water and ice.
the determination of the δD–δ18O relationship in water, and the δD–18O relationship in ice, by mass spectrometric methods.
a method to calculate the best-fit line through the data points of the δ18 O - δD relationship for ice or water.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
least-squares cubic is the most appropriate method for the determination of δ18O– δD relationships for ice or water, and should be used in preference to least-squares linear or functional analysis.
the δ18O and/or δD of a sample should be reported to two significant figures, and the δ18O-δD relationship of a sample set should be summarized with a least-squares cubic fit to the data.
least-squares linear regressions are inappropriate for the δ18O-δD relationship, because the error in both variables is known, and that least-squares cubic regressions should be used instead.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the δD–δ18O slope of the global meteoric water line (GMWL) for precipitation is 8.0 ± 0.3‰.
the least-squares method of regression is the most appropriate for the determination of the δ 18 O-δD relationship.
the δ18O and deuterium (δD) relationship for ice and snow is not linear.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the δ18O and the δD values of ice and water samples are not linearly related and that the δ18 O–δD slope is a function of the δ18 O and the δD value of a given ice or water sample.
it is not appropriate to use a linear regression to summarize the δ18O – δD relationship.
the δ18O and the δD of the snow and the water in a glacier or ice cap are not linearly correlated.
